paper.title: Algorithm 438: Product type two-point Gauss-Legendre-Simpson integration (Collected Algorithms from ACM)

stack: Fortran 77 (netlib TOMS 438.gz shell archive: Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f, driver Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f, Makefile, shipped res)

claim.text: TEST01 of the shipped driver: VINT returned by P2PGS for N = 10 on the integral of F(X)*G(X) with F = 1, G = 1/(1+x**2), is 2.65082 in the shipped res file. Registered by scout from the artifact's own reference output. Tolerance 2e-5 absolute, fixed before any run.
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed integrands in driver.f; no random input)

reference.note: The driver's TEST01 header says the integral is from -1 to 1, but the code (fn00 = 1, gn00 = 1/(1+x*x)) integrates over [-4,4]; its Exact line, 2*atan(4) = 2.65164, uses [-4,4]. The claim is kept as registered and is not changed to fit the header.

attempt: G1: the authors' Makefile in the shipped layout stops at once with 'No rule to make target src.f, needed by src.o' because src.f sits in Fortran/Dp/Src, not beside the Makefile (log kept). The build then runs the Makefile's own rules as separate commands with the src.f path set to ../Src (gfortran 16.2.0, default flags). No source file changed: the pre, mid and post manifests of the authors' sources are identical, so this is a build-only patch. The driver's whole output is identical to the shipped res (diff exit 0), so the N = 10 value matches the reference line for line. Gfortran warnings only.

original_attempt.reason: make stops with 'No rule to make target src.f, needed by src.o': the archive places src.f in ../Src while the Makefile expects it in the same directory.
